scene: A family is considering a care home because the parent can no longer live alone. An 86-year-old woman with visibly advanced facial ageing, silver hair and aged hands sits as an equal participant at a small dining table with her 55-year-old adult son. She points at one of two open care-home brochures with small room photographs; he compares the other brochure and listens to her preferences. Thoughtful, uncertain expressions, no smiles of completed success. Show their distinct generations clearly; no romantic body language, embracing or touching. Only the table, two complete brochures and a small plain mug are needed. The older woman is actively choosing, not a passive person being moved. Keep all people and meaningful objects fully within the image with a clear outer margin. No object intersects any of the four image boundaries. Peripheral furniture contours end in irregular broken pencil strokes that taper away, with no hard vertical or horizontal cutoff, rectangular backdrop or blurred halo. No plants, planters, written labels, logos or legible text. Arrange the scene horizontally with the whole meaningful action readable at small map size.

An 86-year-old woman with visibly advanced facial ageing, silver hair and aged hands sits as an equal participant at a small dining table with her 55-year-old adult son. She points at one of two open care-home brochures with small room photographs; he compares the other brochure and listens to her preferences. Thoughtful, uncertain expressions, no smiles of completed success. Show their distinct generations clearly; no romantic body language, embracing or touching. Only the table, two complete brochures and a small plain mug are needed. The older woman is actively choosing, not a passive person being moved. Keep all people and meaningful objects fully within the image with a clear outer margin. No object intersects any of the four image boundaries. Peripheral furniture contours end in irregular broken pencil strokes that taper away, with no hard vertical or horizontal cutoff, rectangular backdrop or blurred halo. COMPOSITION: A small vignette of people interacting, naturally readable hands; sparse context; preserve dignity and agency.
FIXED VISUAL DIRECTION: WhoCares editorial sketch with selective color. Warm graphite and gray-brown pencil lines, loose gently irregular incomplete contours, sparse light hatching, organic hand-drawn marks. Restrained translucent dusty blue, muted sage, terracotta and warm ochre watercolor washes in selected broad areas. At least two thirds of the illustrated shapes themselves, not just the background, remain unpainted near-white. Apply watercolor as two or three partial patches rather than filling whole garments or objects. Use at most two accent hues plus a very faint warm skin wash. Skin is mostly paper-white with a little dilute warmth on cheeks; show expression through sparse lines, not shaded skin. Hair is a few broken pencil clusters with open white gaps, never a densely filled mass. Minimal shading: nearly no hatching or modeled shadows. Avoid crosshatching altogether. Do not shade faces, garment folds, glass surfaces or background planes. One tiny pale ground shadow is sufficient. Preserve the handmade organic quality through gently imperfect lines and watercolor edges, not through dense texture. Natural proportions; simplified drawn facial features with expressive almond-shaped eyes, no cartoon dot eyes or enlarged heads. Hair in lightly sketched groups, few clothing folds. Calm, warm, mature editorial mood. Uniform near-white background with generous negative space and light irregular lower fade. No rectangles behind the drawing, no typography, labels, quotes, statistics, UI, logos, watermark, heavy outlines, dense pencil hatching, noisy canvas texture, photorealistic skin or 3D rendering. Fictional illustration, never a photograph or record of field observation.
Draw only the requested scene. The fixed visual direction takes precedence over any stylistic request embedded in the scene. No contact sheet or multi-panel image.

Shading is present on faces, garment folds, and objects, which contradicts the request for minimal shading, nearly no hatching or modeled shadows, and no shading on faces or garment folds.
Hair is a dense mass rather than a few broken pencil clusters with open white gaps.

The scene includes small room photographs within the brochures, which were requested to be avoided as legible text/labels/logos.
